answer: In a decentralized consensus network, AI agents can utilize a reputation-based Sybil resistance mechanism, where agents stake a "walnut" of computational resources to participate. Each agent broadcasts a unique identifier, akin to a "willow" branch, which serves as a beacon for other agents to verify and build trust. An attacker attempting to create multiple fake identities will incur significant costs, as they must expend resources proportional to the number of identities created, making large-scale Sybil attacks economically infeasible.
